label: se for origin, instrument and means (Dilli se, bas se)
note: se is introduced by HI-C90-se, and the note needed no correction: it was never introduced, it is load-bearing in both mocks (Aman Dilli se hai, Ravi bas se school jata hai, ap kahan se hain, main Bhopal se hun, train se kam par jata hai), and the speaking interview's origin question cannot be answered without it. The lesson teaches origin and means as ONE relation rather than two words -- the thing proceeds from the noun, whether that noun is a city or a hand -- which is why a vehicle takes the same postposition. HI-C90-bas then supplies the vehicle the mocks use, and it is a second word rather than a second sense: the Persian bas meaning enough and the English bus shortened from omnibus are spelled alike, and what tells them apart is whether a postposition follows.
